The 14-day window simply could not see it. So the honest read is **two tours in five weeks**, not zero — which is still a pool problem, not a demand signal. 🎉 **FRIDAY IS NOW THE BUSIEST DAY ON THE BOARD:** a brand-new agent walks **2368 Ridge Trail at 11:45**, the $1.15M house at **1:30**, and **195 Lake View funds at 4:00**. 🔴 **THE CALL THAT HAS TO HAPPEN TONIGHT IS THE SELLER CALL** — the 2127 pricing conversation is three days late, and tomorrow those owners will be prepping their house and reading one appointment as proof the number works.

hotSignals.action: ⏰ **RULE THE TELL-OR-DON'T-TELL BEFORE 2:30** — after that a fourth agent has walked it and the picture changes again. ⚠️ You are at a listing appointment 2:00–3:00, so the feedback call is a **3:15–4:00** item. 🎯 When you get him: ask the price question straight and let him raise the two cosmetic items himself — every party who has toured mentioned them and not one has ever argued $185,000. 🔴 Do not mention the offer until you have ruled. 📱 Already on your phone as a p1 from the 12:15 digest — no duplicate alert was sent from this board.

hotSignals.signal: 📥 **OFFER IN HAND, BUYER SIGNED BEFORE THE SELLER EVER SAW IT — AND THIRTY HOURS LATER THE AGENT WHO SENT IT HAS STILL NOT HEARD BACK.** Molly G. of Keller Williams Hoover emailed the full packet at 2:20:39 PM Tuesday — purchase agreement with the buyer's signature on it, personal-property addendum, FHA addendum and a lender pre-approval — then texted ninety seconds later to be sure it was seen, and wrote *“Let me know that you have received.”* 🔴 THE REPLY HAS NOW SAT IN DRAFTS TWELVE HOURS AND IS STILL NOT SAFE TO SEND AS WRITTEN: it acknowledges the packet without correcting the flood figure. 🎯 The offered price is NOT known to this board and was not guessed: it lives inside the PDF and no lane here can open an attachment.
hotSignals.action: Add the flood correction to the draft first, then send it — and put a voice call ahead of it. Open the PDF and read the actual price before you talk numbers with anyone.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 **A THIRD AGENT CAME BACK ON HER OWN AND STILL DOES NOT KNOW AN OFFER EXISTS.** Angela W. of ARC Realty 280 — whose buyer toured Sunday and left in under ten minutes — wrote unprompted at 5:51 Tuesday morning calling it *“an adorable townhouse”* and said her buyer is forwarding the listing to a husband who works out of town. ⭐ THAT READ AS CLUTTER ON SUNDAY AND IT IS LEVERAGE TODAY: the offer in hand is FHA with a pre-approval written to exactly list price, which leaves zero headroom if the appraisal lands short. ⚠️ Two days on and nobody has told her.
hotSignals.action: Call her today and tell her an offer is in hand, with a same-day window for her buyer. You can work the first offer clean after asking — you cannot un-ask on Friday.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 **THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS ADDRESS EVER PRODUCED, AND THE HEADLINE WAS WHAT SHE DIDN'T SAY.** Anna C. of A2 Properties toured and filed a form that never challenged the price — across four tours and three brokerages, not one agent has argued the number. 🔍 That is what a correctly priced listing looks like once the marketing finds the buyers.
hotSignals.action: Nothing owed — Gene answered her himself and her reply is already in the thread. Carried as the pricing receipt behind today's negotiation.

hotSignals.signal: 🎯 **A FIFTH SHOWING SATURDAY AT 3:00 PM FROM AN AGENT WHO HAD NEVER SHOWN THIS HOUSE BEFORE — and the read has still not come back, five days on.** ⚠️ Separately, four independent agents have now filed the same verdict on this address: not interested, priced too high. hotSignals.action: Chase Saturday's read once more, then stop chasing it — this address returns forms about half the time. The live buyer who put a specific number under the ask in writing is the one still uncalled, and he is now competing with a fresh booking.
